Deadline reminders configured.value: LMS auto-reminders at 30, 14 and 7 days before the assignment due date, then weekly overdue notices to the learner and their manager; a day-25 alert on new-joiner assignments so the 30-day rule is not missed; a producer overdue extract feeds the commission-hold process monthly

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Course content versions, the role-based curriculum matrix, assignment and completion records with dates and assessment scores, attendance registers for live sessions, and producer acknowledgements retained 5 years from the training date per 31 CFR 1010.430

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Employees or producers overdue past the due date, covered roles missing from the curriculum matrix, content not refreshed after an advisory, and assessment pass marks overridden are logged as training exceptions with root cause, population affected and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every training delinquency campaign and approves any temporary exemption, which must name the individual, the reason and an expiry date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every covered employee on the HRIS worker feed during the year (including joiners, leavers and internal movers) and every producer appointed during the year on the NIPR appointment file, joined to the LMS assignment and completion records

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% completion required for the financial crime team, new business, claims, policy service and executive management; below 98% completion for the wider covered population, any covered role absent from the curriculum matrix, or any new joiner untrained beyond 30 days fails the control

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual with a 30-day new-joiner rule; completion is monitored monthly against the HRIS and appointment feeds and formally tested annually before the board program re-approval

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside both the financial crime function and Learning & Development, and must not have authored or approved the course content

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual AML training completeness workpaper (HRIS-to-LMS reconciliation, producer appointment reconciliation, curriculum-to-risk-assessment mapping, content review, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under BSA-AML / Training / <year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The curriculum matrix, dated course content versions, the completion register by name and date with assessment scores, and producer acknowledgements, producible to a FinCEN or IRS BSA examiner or a state market conduct examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Financial Crime AML Officer answers examiner questions on training adequacy and content; the Learning Development Manager supplies completion extracts; Regulatory Counsel reviews any written representation about coverage before it is sent

checklist.step: Derive the curriculum from the risk assessment and the written controls
actions: Take the current AML risk assessment and list every typology rated medium or high for covered products — single premium from an unexplained source, early surrender accepting the charge, third-party payor, beneficiary change shortly before a claim, 1035 exchange churn.
Map each typology to the written policy or internal control that addresses it and to the learning objective that must teach it.

List the reportable deadlines the course must state plainly: CTR within 15 calendar days of the reportable currency transaction under 31 CFR 1010.311 and 1010.313(b), SAR within 30 calendar days of initial detection or 60 where no suspect is identified under 1025.320.
Write the curriculum design note showing typology, control, learning objective and the target roles, and route it to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every medium and high typology maps to a written control and a learning objective, and the design note is approved.

checklist.step: Define the covered population role by role
actions: Extract the active worker list with job code, department, cost centre, manager and hire date.

Tag each job code as covered or not covered against the curriculum matrix, covering new business, policy service, claims, billing, contact centre, financial crime, internal audit and executive management.
Set up a nightly feed of joiners, leavers and internal movers into the LMS so a mover into a covered role picks up the assignment automatically.
Send the tagged job-code list to the Financial Crime AML Officer for confirmation and record their approval.
checklist.done: every active job code carries a covered/not-covered tag approved by the AML Officer and a nightly mover feed reaches the LMS.

checklist.step: Build the role-based modules with covered-product content
actions: Build a core module for all covered staff: what BSA/AML is, which products are covered under 31 CFR 1025.100(h), the four filing bases, the $5,000 aggregate and the any-amount insider rule, and the no-tipping-off prohibition.

Build role modules: new business and underwriting (source of funds, third-party payor, entity owners), policy service (beneficiary change red flags, assignment screening), claims (payee screening before disbursement, beneficiary change proximity to claim), billing (overpayment then refund to a different account, cash-equivalent instruments).

State the deadlines explicitly on screen — CTR within 15 calendar days, SAR within 30 calendar days of initial detection or 60 where no suspect is identified — and require the learner to answer a question on each.
Include the escalation route by name: raise an Unusual Activity Referral into the AML case queue, never discuss it with the customer or the producer.
Version the content with an effective date and store the source files in the document management repository.
checklist.done: core and role modules are built with covered-product red flags, the named deadlines and the escalation route, and are versioned with an effective date.

checklist.step: Get the content reviewed by compliance and counsel before release
actions: Read the module scripts against 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(1) and (b)(3) and confirm each required element is taught, not merely mentioned.
Check every regulatory citation, threshold and day count on screen against the current e-CFR text and correct any stale figure.
Confirm the confidentiality module states the 31 CFR 1025.320(d) prohibition correctly and does not encourage staff to record SAR references in customer systems.
Record the review date, the reviewer and the content version approved, and release only the approved version to the LMS.
checklist.done: the released content version carries a dated counsel and compliance review with every citation and day count verified.

checklist.step: Assign the courses and set the due dates
actions: Create the annual assignment rule for every covered job code with a due date of 31 December and open the window at the start of the annual cycle.
Create the joiner rule setting a due date of hire date plus 30 days for anyone entering a covered job code, including internal movers.
Configure reminder notifications at 30, 14 and 7 days before due date, then weekly overdue notices copied to the learner's manager.
Run a dry-run assignment against the HRIS extract and reconcile assignment count to covered headcount before going live.
checklist.done: assignments exist for every covered worker with the correct due date, reminders are configured, and assignment count reconciles to covered headcount.

checklist.step: Deliver and record training for appointed producers
actions: Extract the appointed producer list by NPN and state from the appointment file and reconcile it to NIPR appointment records for the year.
Publish the producer AML course on the agent portal and require completion within 30 days of appointment and annually thereafter before new business is accepted.

Accept an industry-standard AML course certificate (for example a LIMRA AML certificate) as an alternative, and record the certificate provider, completion date and certificate number against the producer record.
Capture a signed acknowledgement that the producer will refer red flags and will not disclose a referral to the customer.
Send the monthly overdue producer list to the Commission Analyst so commissions are held until completion.
checklist.done: every appointed producer has a completion record or an accepted certificate on file, with overdue producers on commission hold.

checklist.step: Assess understanding rather than attendance
actions: Attach a scored assessment of at least 10 questions to each module with an 80% pass mark and a randomised question bank.
Include scenario questions that require the learner to pick the correct deadline — 15 calendar days for a CTR, 30 calendar days from initial detection for a SAR — and the correct escalation route.
Allow two retakes; a third failure routes the learner to the Financial Crime AML Officer for a coached session recorded on the LMS record.
Report question-level failure rates to the Financial Crime AML Officer so weak content can be rewritten.
checklist.done: each module has a scored 80% pass-mark assessment, retake and coaching path, and question-level failure rates are reported.

checklist.step: Deliver enhanced training to the financial crime team and senior management
actions: Run a live annual session for the financial crime team covering SAR narrative writing to the FinCEN standard, the BSA E-Filing form 111 field-by-field walkthrough, and the 120-day continuing-activity review.
Run a separate briefing for the board and executive committee covering their 31 CFR 1025.210 responsibilities, the year's SAR and sanctions volumes and the independent test findings.
Cover the CTR path for the rare cash-equivalent premium receipt — the 15-calendar-day filing deadline under 31 CFR 1010.311 and 1010.313(b) and who files it.
Take a signed attendance register at each session and load it to the LMS against the individual records so live delivery is evidenced like e-learning.
Record the session date, content version and facilitator in the training evidence folder.
checklist.done: the financial crime team and the board have dated live sessions with signed attendance registers loaded to their LMS records.

checklist.step: Track completion monthly against the live worker feed
actions: Publish a monthly completion dashboard by department, job family and manager, sourced from the LMS and the HRIS worker feed on the same date.
Show completed, in progress, not started and overdue counts, and highlight any covered worker with no assignment at all — that is a matrix gap, not a delinquency.
Reconcile the dashboard headcount to the HRIS active headcount and explain any difference on the dashboard footer.
Send each department head their overdue list with names and due dates on the first business day of the month.
checklist.done: the monthly dashboard reconciles to HRIS headcount, exposes unassigned covered workers and puts named overdue lists with department heads.

checklist.step: Escalate delinquency with consequences that bite
actions: At 15 days overdue escalate to the learner's manager; at 30 days to the department head; at 45 days to the executive committee member for that function.
For producers, instruct the Commission Analyst to hold commission payments and suspend new business acceptance at 30 days overdue.
For employees in the financial crime, claims and new business teams, agree with the HR Business Partner that system access to covered-product transactions is reviewed at 45 days overdue.
Approve any exemption in writing, naming the individual, the reason and an expiry date no more than 60 days out.
checklist.done: delinquency escalates on the 15/30/45-day ladder with commission holds for producers and every exemption is named, reasoned and time-limited.

checklist.step: Run targeted training after an incident or advisory
actions: On each FinCEN advisory, independent test finding or internal incident, decide within 10 business days whether targeted training is needed and record the decision.
Where it is, define the affected population precisely (for example claims examiners who released payouts without a current screen) and the specific behaviour to change.
Have the Instructional Designer build a short module or a live session and deliver it within 60 days of the advisory or finding.
Record attendance and assessment results against the incident or finding so the corrective action can be evidenced as closed.
checklist.done: each advisory, finding or incident has a dated training decision and, where needed, delivery inside 60 days linked to the corrective action.

checklist.step: Refresh content annually against the current typologies
actions: Before the annual cycle opens, compare the course content to the refreshed risk assessment, the year's SAR typologies and the independent test findings.
Rewrite any scenario that no longer reflects the business — for example after a new annuity product launch or a block acquisition.
Re-verify every citation, threshold and day count against the current e-CFR text and update where FinCEN has amended the rule.
Route the refreshed version through counsel review and record the new content version and effective date.
checklist.done: the content version released for the new cycle is dated, reflects the current risk assessment and typologies, and has verified citations.

checklist.step: Feed training outcomes back into the written controls
actions: Take the question-level failure rates, learner questions and post-incident training findings and identify controls that staff cannot execute as written.
Where a procedure is the cause, raise a change to the written policy or internal control in the GRC policy module with the training evidence attached.
Confirm the changed procedure is reflected in the next content version so the course and the procedure never diverge.
Record the loop — finding, procedure change, content change — in the annual program review pack.
checklist.done: every recurring assessment failure or learner confusion results in either a procedure change or a content change, recorded in the review pack.

checklist.step: Report training coverage to the AML Oversight Committee and the board
actions: Report annual completion by covered population and by producer channel, new-joiner 30-day compliance, average assessment score and open exemptions.
Show completion against the 100% and 98% thresholds by name of function, not as a single blended number.
Present open training exceptions with owner and remediation date and seek the committee's acceptance or rejection of any extension.
Include the training section in the annual board program submission so re-approval rests on evidenced coverage.
checklist.done: completion is reported by function against its threshold, exceptions are tabled with owners, and the training section forms part of the board submission.

checklist.step: Retain training evidence for five years
actions: Export the annual completion register (name, worker or NPN id, job code, module, version, completion date, assessment score) and file it under BSA-AML / Training / <year>.
File the dated course content versions, the curriculum matrix, live-session attendance registers and producer acknowledgements alongside it.
Apply the 5-year retention label measured from the training date, per 31 CFR 1010.430(d).
Confirm the index supports retrieval by individual name, NPN, module version and completion date, and run an annual retrieval test on 5 records.
checklist.done: the completion register, content versions and acknowledgements are filed under a 5-year label and retrievable by name, NPN and module version.

testing.step: Build the covered-population training obligation register
actions: Extract every worker active at any point in the year with job code, hire date, termination date and internal move history.
Extract every producer appointed during the year with NPN, appointment date and state from the appointment file.
Apply the approved covered/not-covered job-code tagging to build the obligation register, and reconcile the register headcount to the HRIS active headcount and the NIPR appointment count.
testing.done: the obligation register reconciles to HRIS headcount and the NIPR appointment count and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the obligation register to LMS assignments and completions
actions: Left-join the obligation register to the LMS assignment table on worker id or NPN and list every covered person with no assignment.
Join again to the completion table and list every assignment not completed by its due date, with days overdue.
Compute completion percentages by function and compare to the 100% and 98% thresholds.
Treat a covered person with no assignment as a control design failure, not a delinquency, and report it separately.
testing.done: unassigned covered people, overdue assignments and by-function completion rates are quantified against the thresholds.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of the financial crime team, 100% of new joiners into covered roles and 100% of approved exemptions.
Take 30 employees and 20 producers by seeded random selection from the remaining covered population.
Record the seed, the strata, the population sizes and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers the whole financial crime team, all new joiners and all exemptions plus a random draw.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day new-joiner and annual deadlines
actions: For each sampled new joiner or internal mover, recompute the due date as hire or move date plus 30 calendar days and compare it to the LMS completion date.
For the annual cycle, confirm each sampled completion date falls on or before 31 December of the training year.
For producers, recompute appointment date plus 30 days and compare to the completion or certificate date.
Log every completion after the recomputed deadline as an exception with the day count, not as a rounding difference.
testing.done: every sampled deadline is recomputed from the source date and on-time or late is concluded with a day count.

testing.step: Test the curriculum against the risk assessment and the rule
actions: Take the current risk assessment's medium and high typologies for covered products and confirm each is taught in at least one module assigned to the roles that would encounter it.
Read the released content version and confirm it states the CTR 15-calendar-day deadline, the SAR 30-calendar-day deadline and the 60-day no-suspect extension correctly.
Confirm the confidentiality content states the 31 CFR 1025.320(d) prohibition and that the escalation route names the AML case queue.
Flag any typology with no coverage and any stale citation or day count as a content finding.
testing.done: every medium and high typology is evidenced in an assigned module and every stated deadline and citation is verified as current.

testing.step: Verify completion records back to their evidence
actions: For sampled employees, open the LMS record and confirm the module version, completion timestamp and assessment score are present and the score meets the 80% pass mark.
For live sessions, trace the completion flag to the signed attendance register rather than accepting the LMS flag alone.
For producers relying on an external certificate, open the certificate and confirm the provider, the producer name and NPN, and the completion date.
Flag any completion recorded by an administrator override with no underlying evidence.
testing.done: each sampled completion traces to an assessment score, a signed attendance register or an inspected external certificate.

testing.step: Test delinquency escalation and exemption discipline
actions: For each overdue case in the population, confirm the 15/30/45-day escalation notices were actually sent and to whom.
For overdue producers, confirm the commission hold was applied and the date it took effect, and check whether new business was accepted while overdue.
Read every approved exemption and confirm it names the individual, the reason and an expiry no more than 60 days out, with the Head of Compliance's signature.
Treat any expired exemption still relied on as an exception.
testing.done: escalation notices, commission holds and time-limited signed exemptions are evidenced for every overdue case.

testing.step: Test the post-advisory and post-incident training loop
actions: List every FinCEN advisory, independent test finding and internal AML incident in the year.
For each, confirm a dated decision on targeted training exists within 10 business days and, where training was required, that delivery occurred within 60 days.
Trace the attendance record back to the corrective action so the action's closure rests on evidenced delivery.
Flag any corrective action closed on a training commitment with no delivery evidence.
testing.done: every advisory, finding and incident has a dated training decision and, where required, evidenced delivery inside 60 days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception — unassigned covered role, late new joiner, overdue producer, stale content citation, unevidenced completion, expired exemption — with the population affected.
Assign a root cause (job-code tagging gap, HRIS-to-LMS feed break, appointment file not reconciled to NIPR, content review calendar missed) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and require a completion sweep where a whole role or channel was unassigned.
Carry every open exception into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with the affected population, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the training test
actions: Compute completion by function against the 100% and 98% thresholds and the new-joiner 30-day compliance rate.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each figure.
Have the Internal Auditor, who sits outside financial crime and Learning & Development and authored none of the content, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion to the AML Oversight Committee before the board's annual program re-approval and file the signed workpaper under BSA-AML / Training.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with by-function completion rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed before board re-approval.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns delivery of the independent AML test required by 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(4), its reporting to senior management and the Audit Committee, and the tracking of corrective actions to documented closure; reports functionally to the Audit Committee, not to the AML function

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(4) requiring independent testing by company personnel or an outside party, read with 1025.210(b)(1), re-verified in the current e-CFR at scoping, and benchmarked to the FFIEC BSA/AML Examination Manual testing modules used to shape the work programme

In-scope processes.value: Independent testing of the whole AML program for covered products — the risk assessment, written policies and internal controls, the designated officer's authority, transaction monitoring and thresholds, OFAC screening, SAR timeliness and quality, training coverage, recordkeeping and prior-year action closure

In-scope systems.value: The engagement, work programme, workpapers, findings, ratings and management actions with owners and dates are held in AuditBoard; evidence is pulled from Actimize, the screening system, the LMS, the case system and the policy administration platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Independent AML Testing Procedure — annual risk-based scoping, independence declaration, the work programme covering each 1025.210(b) pillar plus 1025.320, sampling standard, finding severity definitions, reporting route to senior management and the Audit Committee, and the corrective-action closure evidence standard

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Audit Committee as part of the annual audit plan, re-approved annually, and amended when the risk assessment or a regulatory examination changes the required scope

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Testing performed at least annually and completed before the board's annual AML program re-approval; the report issued to senior management within 30 days of fieldwork close; management actions agreed within 30 days of report issue; high-severity actions remediated within 90 days of agreement

Deadline reminders configured.value: AuditBoard raises reminders at 60 and 30 days before the annual testing due date, chases action owners at 30, 14 and 7 days before each action due date, and escalates any high-severity action passing its due date to the Chief Audit Executive the next business day

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The scoping memo, independence declaration, work programme, workpapers and samples, the issued report, senior management and Audit Committee minutes, and the action closure evidence retained 5 years from the report date per 31 CFR 1010.430

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Testing not performed in the year, scope areas dropped without Audit Committee approval, findings closed without evidence, and actions extended more than twice are logged as testing-process exceptions with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every high-severity finding after inspecting the remediation evidence, and approves any extension of an action due date with a written reason

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The prior and current year AML test engagements, every finding raised and every management action open at any point in the year, plus the scope areas required by 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(1)-(4) and 1025.320 mapped to the work programme

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a year with no independent test, on any pillar of 1025.210(b) left untested without Audit Committee approval, and on any finding closed with no evidence attached; more than 20% of high-severity actions past due, or any action extended more than twice, fails the control

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual; the quality-assurance review of the testing process runs annually after report issue, with quarterly action-ageing reviews at the Audit Committee between engagements

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be outside Internal Audit and must not have performed any fieldwork; where the annual test is outsourced, the reviewer challenges the provider's independence and scope

Evidence location for test results.value: The AML independent testing engagement file in AuditBoard, with the issued report, workpapers, action tracker export and Audit Committee minute extract copied to the compliance evidence repository under BSA-AML / Independent Testing / <year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The scoping memo, independence declaration, work programme, issued report with ratings, management responses with owners and dates, and closure evidence, producible to a FinCEN or IRS SB/SE BSA examiner within 5 business days as the 1025.210(b)(4) evidence pack

Regulator response path.value: Chief Audit Executive presents the testing methodology and findings to examiners; the Financial Crime AML Officer answers on remediation status; Regulatory Counsel reviews any written response and the Audit Committee chair is briefed before submission

checklist.step: Scope the annual test from the risk assessment and prior findings
actions: Read the current AML risk assessment, the prior year's report, open management actions and any regulatory examination findings, and list the areas rated medium or high.
Draft the scoping memo covering each pillar of 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(1)-(4) plus 1025.320 SAR reporting and OFAC screening, and state the coverage depth for each.
Justify in writing any pillar covered by reliance on other work rather than direct testing; a pillar cannot be dropped without Audit Committee approval.
Set the fieldwork window so the report issues before the board's annual AML program re-approval date.
Table the scoping memo at the Audit Committee and record its approval.
checklist.done: an Audit Committee-approved scoping memo covers every 1025.210(b) pillar and 1025.320, with any reliance justified and the timing tied to board re-approval.

checklist.step: Establish and document independence
actions: Have every assigned auditor sign an independence declaration confirming they have not worked in the financial crime function, designed AML controls or adjudicated alerts in the last 12 months.
Confirm the engagement reports to the Audit Committee and that the Financial Crime AML Officer has no role in staffing, scoping, rating or issuing the report.
Where the work is outsourced, obtain the provider's independence confirmation, the lead reviewer's BSA/AML credentials and confirm the provider does not also build or tune the company's AML controls.
File the declarations in the engagement file before fieldwork starts.
checklist.done: signed independence declarations are on file for every reviewer before fieldwork, and the reporting line to the Audit Committee is documented.

checklist.step: Build the work programme from the rule text
actions: Write one test step per requirement: written policies and internal controls (b)(1), designated officer (b)(2), training (b)(3), independent testing history (b)(4), and SAR detection and filing (1025.320).
For each step state the population, the sampling method and size, the evidence to inspect and the pass criteria before fieldwork begins.
Add steps for OFAC screening completeness, monitoring feed integrity, threshold change control and the 5-year recordkeeping requirement.
Have the Chief Audit Executive approve the work programme and lock it so scope changes require a documented amendment.
checklist.done: the approved work programme carries one test step per statutory requirement with population, sample and pass criteria stated in advance.

checklist.step: Test the program design against the rule and the risk assessment
actions: Read the board-approved AML program and confirm every clause of 1025.210(b) maps to a named procedure, owner and evidence artifact.
Confirm the board resolution designating the AML officer is current, names SAR-filing authority and covers every day of the period.
Trace each medium and high typology in the risk assessment to a detection scenario, a control or an accepted risk decision.
Confirm the covered/not-covered product determinations carry citations and that new products passed the AML design gate before first issue.
checklist.done: each statutory clause, typology and product determination is traced to a documented control or an evidenced acceptance.

checklist.step: Test SAR and screening operation on a documented sample
actions: Draw a seeded sample of cases, filings and screening alerts, recording seed, population size and strata in the workpaper.
Recompute the 30/60-calendar-day SAR clock from the underlying detection evidence and compare it to the BSA E-Filing acknowledgement date.
Re-screen sampled parties against the OFAC list version in force at the original screen date and re-adjudicate a sample of closed false positives.
Record each re-performance conclusion in the workpaper with the evidence captured, before reading the original disposition.
checklist.done: sampled SAR clocks and screening decisions are independently re-performed with captured evidence and a documented, reproducible sample.

checklist.step: Test training coverage and recordkeeping
actions: Reconcile the HRIS covered-population extract and the NIPR producer appointment list to LMS assignments and completions and quantify the gaps.
Recompute the 30-day new-joiner deadline for sampled joiners and compare to the completion date.

Test retention by requesting five records at random — a filed SAR with its acknowledgement, a screening log, a program version, a completion register and a blocked-property report — and record whether each came back inside one business day.
Confirm the retention labels applied match the 5-year requirement measured from the correct start date.
checklist.done: training gaps are quantified, joiner deadlines recomputed, and a live retrieval test proves the 5-year records come back.

checklist.step: Write findings with severity, cause and regulatory consequence
actions: Write each finding as condition, criteria (the exact CFR cite), cause, effect and recommendation, with the workpaper reference attached.
Rate severity against the defined scale: high where a statutory requirement is not met or a filing was late, medium where the control operates but with gaps, low for documentation.
Quantify the population affected — transactions unmonitored, payouts unscreened, filings late, staff untrained — rather than describing it qualitatively.
Validate the factual accuracy of each finding with the Financial Crime AML Officer without ceding control of the rating.
checklist.done: every finding carries condition, CFR criteria, cause, effect, a quantified population, a severity rating and a workpaper reference.

checklist.step: Agree management actions with named owners and dates
actions: Respond to each finding with a specific action, a named individual owner and a due date — 90 days from agreement for high-severity findings.
Reject 'noted' or 'accepted' as a response; where the risk is genuinely accepted, escalate the acceptance to the Chief Risk Officer for written approval.
State the evidence that will prove closure — a rerun report, a configuration screenshot, a completion register — at the point the action is agreed, not at closure.
Load actions into the tracker within 30 days of report issue.
checklist.done: every finding has an owned, dated action in the tracker with the closure evidence defined up front, loaded within 30 days of issue.

checklist.step: Deliver the report to senior management and the Audit Committee
actions: Issue the report within 30 days of fieldwork close to the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Risk Officer, Head of Compliance and Financial Crime AML Officer.
Table it at the Audit Committee with the overall program opinion, the finding count by severity and the prior-year action status.
Minute the committee's challenge and any direction, including any instruction to re-test an area, and publish the pack to the board portal.
Confirm the board sees the report before it re-approves the AML program, so re-approval is informed by the testing outcome.
checklist.done: the report is issued within 30 days of fieldwork close, minuted at the Audit Committee, and seen by the board before program re-approval.

checklist.step: Track corrective actions to their due dates
actions: Run the action tracker weekly and chase owners at 30, 14 and 7 days before due date.
Escalate any high-severity action passing its due date to the Chief Audit Executive the next business day with the owner named.
Require a written reason and a Chief Audit Executive approval for any extension; a second extension escalates to the Audit Committee, and a third is not permitted.
Publish an action-ageing report to the AML Oversight Committee each quarter showing open, overdue and extended counts by severity.
checklist.done: actions are chased on the 30/14/7-day ladder, overdue high-severity items escalate next business day and extensions carry written approvals.

checklist.step: Validate remediation evidence before closing a finding
actions: Inspect the evidence named at agreement — the rerun monitoring report, the screening configuration screenshot, the updated procedure version, the completion register — rather than accepting the owner's assertion.
Re-perform a small sample of the remediated control: for a threshold fix, re-run the aggregation on 5 parties; for a screening gap, re-screen 5 payouts.
Where the evidence does not demonstrate the fix, reopen the action with a new due date and record why it failed validation.
Record the validation date, the evidence reference and the validator on the action before closure.
checklist.done: no finding closes without inspected evidence, a small re-performance and a named validator recorded on the action.

checklist.step: Sign off closure of high-severity findings
actions: Review the validation evidence personally for every high-severity finding and record the sign-off date on the action.
Confirm the underlying regulatory exposure is closed, not merely documented — a late SAR finding closes only when the timeliness metric has held for two consecutive months.
Report closures and remaining open high-severity items to the Audit Committee each quarter.
Carry any unclosed high-severity finding into the next year's scope as a mandatory retest area.
checklist.done: every high-severity closure carries a personal CAE sign-off resting on sustained metric evidence, with open items carried into next year's scope.

checklist.step: Escalate a year with no test or a dropped scope area
actions: Compare the scoping memo's covered areas to the work actually performed and list any pillar of 1025.210(b) that went untested.
Where testing did not occur in the year, raise it immediately to the Audit Committee chair as a breach of 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(4), not as a plan slippage.
Record the exposure period and require a catch-up engagement with a committed completion date.
Log the issue in the GRC platform with root cause and owner and report it in the annual board program submission.
checklist.done: any untested pillar or missed year is raised to the Audit Committee chair as a regulatory breach with a committed catch-up date.

checklist.step: Report the testing outcome into the board program re-approval
actions: Prepare the testing section of the annual board program submission: the opinion, finding counts by severity, prior-year closure rate and open high-severity items.
State plainly whether the program as operated meets each requirement of 31 CFR 1025.210(b) and 1025.320.
Recommend to the board any condition attached to re-approval, such as a re-test date for an unclosed high-severity area.
Record the board's decision and any conditions in the engagement file.
checklist.done: the board re-approval pack carries a stated per-requirement opinion, open high-severity items and any re-approval conditions, all minuted.

checklist.step: Retain the engagement file for five years
actions: Export the engagement file — scoping memo, independence declarations, work programme, workpapers with samples and seeds, issued report, management responses, action tracker and closure evidence — from AuditBoard.
File it under BSA-AML / Independent Testing / <year> together with the Audit Committee minute extract.
Apply the 5-year retention label measured from the report issue date, per 31 CFR 1010.430(d).
Confirm the index supports retrieval by report year, finding id and CFR citation, and run an annual retrieval test on the prior two engagements.
checklist.done: the full engagement file is exported, filed under a 5-year label and retrievable by report year, finding id and CFR citation.

testing.step: Build the population of engagements, findings and actions
actions: Extract the AML testing engagements for the current and prior year with scoping dates, fieldwork dates and report issue dates.
Extract every finding raised with severity, CFR citation, owner, due date, extensions and closure date, and every action open at any point in the year.
Reconcile the finding and action counts to the Audit Committee packs tabled during the year and resolve any difference before sampling.
testing.done: the engagement, finding and action population reconciles to the Audit Committee packs and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the work performed to the approved scope
actions: Map each work programme step to the requirement it covers — 1025.210(b)(1), (b)(2), (b)(3), (b)(4) and 1025.320 — plus OFAC screening and recordkeeping.
List any pillar with no completed step, and check whether the Audit Committee approved the omission in the minutes.
Confirm the fieldwork close and report issue dates fall before the board's AML program re-approval date.
Treat an untested pillar with no minuted approval as an automatic control failure.
testing.done: every statutory pillar maps to a completed step or a minuted committee approval, and the timing precedes board re-approval.

testing.step: Draw and document the finding and action sample
actions: Take 100% of high-severity findings, 100% of actions extended more than once and 100% of findings closed in the year.
Take 15 medium and low findings by seeded random selection from the remainder.
Record the seed, the strata, the population sizes and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all high-severity findings, all extended actions and all closures plus a random draw.

testing.step: Test independence of the reviewers who performed the work
actions: Read each assigned reviewer's signed independence declaration and check the date precedes fieldwork start.
Cross-check the reviewer names against the HRIS position history and the AML case system for any alert adjudication or control design in the last 12 months.
Where the work was outsourced, confirm the provider does not also build, tune or operate any AML control for the company.
Confirm the Financial Crime AML Officer had no role in staffing, scoping, rating or issuing the report.
testing.done: every reviewer's independence is evidenced by a pre-fieldwork declaration corroborated against position and case history.

testing.step: Re-perform sampled test steps to confirm the conclusion holds
actions: For five sampled work programme steps, re-draw the sample from the recorded seed and confirm it reproduces the same rows.
Re-perform two steps end to end — for example recompute a SAR 30-day clock and re-screen a payout party — and compare to the recorded conclusion.
Confirm each workpaper holds the evidence it cites rather than a reference to evidence held elsewhere.
Flag any conclusion the underlying evidence does not support, including 'no exceptions noted' on a step with no visible testing.
testing.done: sampled steps reproduce from their seeds, two re-performed steps agree with the recorded conclusion, and unsupported conclusions are flagged.

testing.step: Test finding quality, severity and quantification
actions: Check each sampled finding states condition, criteria with the exact CFR cite, cause, effect and recommendation.
Confirm severity follows the defined scale — a late SAR filing or an untested pillar cannot be rated medium or low.
Confirm the population affected is quantified in numbers and value rather than described qualitatively.
Flag any finding downgraded after management review with no documented rationale.
testing.done: every sampled finding is complete, correctly rated against the scale and quantified, with any downgrade documented.

testing.step: Recompute the reporting and remediation deadline maths
actions: Recompute report issue date minus fieldwork close date and compare to the 30-day standard.
Recompute action load date minus report issue date and compare to the 30-day standard.
For high-severity findings, recompute agreement date plus 90 days and compare to the actual closure date, counting each extension separately.
Compute the percentage of high-severity actions past due at year end and compare to the 20% threshold.
testing.done: issue, load and remediation intervals are recomputed against the 30/30/90-day standards and the past-due percentage is measured against 20%.

testing.step: Inspect the evidence behind every sampled closure
actions: Open each sampled closed action and inspect the evidence attached against the closure evidence defined when the action was agreed.
Confirm a named validator other than the action owner recorded the validation date.
For high-severity closures, confirm the Chief Audit Executive sign-off exists and rests on sustained metric evidence rather than a single point-in-time artefact.
Reopen in the tracker any closure whose evidence does not demonstrate the fix, and record the reason.
testing.done: every sampled closure has evidence matching the agreed standard, a segregated validator and, for high severity, a CAE sign-off on sustained evidence.

testing.step: Log testing-process exceptions with root cause, owner and date
actions: Raise one issue per exception — pillar untested, independence not evidenced, finding under-rated, action closed without evidence, action extended more than twice, report issued late.
Assign a root cause (audit resourcing, scope negotiated down, closure evidence standard not defined at agreement, tracker discipline) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a statutory pillar went untested, require a catch-up engagement with a committed date.
Carry every open exception into the next annual quality review as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for untested pillars, a committed catch-up engagement.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the quality review of the AML test
actions: Compute pillar coverage, the closure-evidence pass rate and the percentage of high-severity actions past due against the zero-tolerance and 20% thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each figure.
Sign the workpaper as the independent reviewer, confirming no involvement in the fieldwork under review.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee alongside the annual AML test report and file the signed workpaper under BSA-AML / Independent Testing.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with pillar coverage, closure-evidence pass rate, a stated conclusion and an Audit Committee reporting date is on file.
